title: Re-deliver governed active Work Item synchronization on current main
rawUserRequest: Continue executing the authorized remediation plan to completion; when a workflow problem is discovered, create a corrective Work Item rather than applying a temporary workaround.

declaredIntent.summary: Deliver the governed synchronization capability from immutable #691 evidence onto current main without rebasing, rewriting, or otherwise mutating #691/#698.

outOfScope: Rebasing, merging, force-pushing, closing, deleting, or otherwise mutating archived Work Item #691, its archive evidence, its branch, or PR #698
Any provider or remote Git mutation outside the normal successor PR lifecycle
Using the new synchronization capability for #663 before this successor is merged
Changing #663 implementation or its provider state in this Work Item
Weakening Start Receipt, ancestry, clean-worktree, scope, predecessor, or evidence-integrity validation
Updating a security baseline to conceal new findings

riskAssessment.reason: A successor must reproduce an audited local-Git lifecycle capability on a newer main while preserving immutable predecessor evidence and maintaining source/template parity.

reasons: The user authorized automatic corrective Work Items; this changes lifecycle evidence, Git safety controls, installed templates, and canonical documentation.

override.approvalEvidence: The user granted standing authorization for required Work Item corrections, lifecycle completion, and provider operations in this thread.
override.reason: Strict lifecycle and evidence-integrity verification without a release operation.
notRunChecks: Release-preflight and distribution verification are inapplicable because this Work Item neither changes release-owned resources nor publishes.

executionDecision.reason: #699 provides an explicit corrective successor on current main; #691/#698 will remain immutable and no temporary or manual lifecycle bypass will be used.

preReviewWarnings: Review predecessor immutability, source binding, ancestry, dirty-state rejection, replay rejection, executable-path safety, and source/template documentation parity.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Lifecycle and Git-history changes require immutable before-edit and before-finish checkpoints.

acceptance: The successor begins from base commit 9d2fe82ebdb907dd9375cbc255e0b7c64e4d8b76 and re-delivers only #691's governed synchronization capability; #691 archive evidence, branch, and PR #698 remain unchanged.

`make ai-synchronize-work-item CONTRACT=<active-contract> BASE_REMOTE=<remote> BASE_BRANCH=<default>` performs an eligible local dedicated-branch rebase onto the exact remote default target and atomically records old/new base, branch/worktree identity, Contract/Summary digests, and append-only transition evidence.

Before rebase, the command rejects dirty, archived, detached/base branch, foreign Work Item, stale remote, non-ancestor, provider-mutated, unrelated, or already-synchronized states; it never pushes, force-pushes, opens a PR, mutates provider state, changes immutable Start Receipt, or rewrites archive evidence.

A rebase conflict is aborted automatically and leaves active Contract/Summary and lifecycle evidence byte-identical; a successful rebase invalidates prior verification and requires fresh preflight plus current-generation checks before Finish.

Regression tests cover a legal synchronization, conflict abort, all pre-rebase rejection boundaries, replay/stale evidence, and absolute governed Git executable handling without adding Bandit findings beyond the repository baseline.

Canonical lifecycle/workflow/Cockpit documentation and installed-template counterparts document the exact command, authority limits, recovery conditions, and parity; canonical generated capability and documentation-alignment evidence is refreshed.

The successor produces a red/yellow/green Outcome through normal `ai-finish`, is archived only after all gates pass, receives a clean merged PR, and closes through the merged-PR lifecycle before #663 consumes the capability.
guidelines: Keep the command narrower than Git rebase: establish only a verified local baseline transition and never mutate refs or provider state.
Preserve immutable Start Receipt and predecessor/archive facts; use append-only, digest-bound transition evidence.
Maintain source-template-installed runtime parity for every public lifecycle command and its recovery documentation.
New public command behavior, authority limits, and recovery conditions must be documented in canonical lifecycle guidance.
Use source-level subprocess safety controls and focused tests; do not mask security findings through baseline changes.

intent.problem: #691 completed and was archived with a warning-free Outcome, but its draft PR #698 became DIRTY after #687 merged. Policy prohibits rebasing or rewriting archived evidence, leaving an approved capability unavailable on current main.
constraints: Start from the latest current main and preserve #691/#698 as immutable audit evidence.
The command may perform only a verified local rebase; provider and remote Git mutations remain outside its authority.
Dedicated identity, clean state, target ancestry, and Contract/Summary/Start Receipt integrity are required before any active-evidence write.
A baseline transition invalidates verification and never makes Finish eligible.
Source, installed template, canonical docs, and generated truth artifacts must remain aligned.
intent.rationale: A successor applies the already-approved governed behavior to current main without corrupting audit history or normalizing a manual rebase workaround.

scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Exercise each invalid fixture and assert errors plus byte-for-byte no-write postconditions.
